rows.author: F057
rows.title_full: THE INVESTMENTS AND INCENTIVES CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Proposes provisions regarding: Organization and Functions of the Board of Investment; Establishment of Domestic Industrial Zones; Investment with Incentives (Qualified Activities, Incentives to Registered Enterprises, Availment of Incentives, Registration of Enterprises, Basic Rights and Guarantees of Registered Enterprises, Administration of Incentives, and others.
Defines several terms, among others as Investments Promotion Agencies (IPAS), Investments Priorities Plan (IPP), Export Sales of Goods/Services, Export/Domestic Enterprise, Domestic Industrial Zone, Special Economic Zone, Domestic Industrial Zone Developer, Export Processing Zone, Supply Chain City, and Capital Equipment.
Seeks to streamline the tax breaks for businesses by stopping the practice of having perpetual perks for several industries; Intends to grant tax breaks to exporters and limits the income tax holiday for domestic enterprises to four years; Provides for an investment policy that will improve the country´s investment programs and strategies and ensuring that no industry will unjustly benefit from the incentives to be provided.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RATIONALIZATION OF WAGE LEVELS ON A NATIONAL AND INDUSTRIAL BASIS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Proposes to institute the rationalization of wage levels on a per industry basis instead of the current regional minimum wage structure in order to achieve an equitable pay between workers in the regions, and which will ensure responsiveness to peculiarities unique to each industry.

Seeks therefore to abolish the existing Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Boards and instead 
empower the National Wages and Productivity Commission to determine and fix the minimum wage rates to address regional wage distortions.

rows.author: J021
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING BROADER PROTECTION TO CONSUMERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7394, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `CONSUMER ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES´
rows.abstract:
Intends to increase penalties and sanctions on unscrupulous, deceitful, and dishonest merchants; and to endeavor for the integration and utilization of ICT to conform with the current trends in the market.
Proposes for the following amendments, among others:
Definition of terms, among others: “BUSINESS NAME, FIRM NAME, OR STYLE”  to include ANY ELECTRONIC EVIDENCE OF AGREEMENT, BUSINESS TRANSACTION OR ADVERTISEMENT THROUGH INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY (ICT) MEDIA, INCLUDING VOICE, VIDEO, AND OTHER FORMS OF DATA; “MASS MEDIA” to include INTERNET, MOBILE PHONE, LANDLINE as additional means or methods to convey advertising messages; Publication of consumer product standards in THE OFFICIAL GAZETTE OR IN THE DEPARTMENT´S OFFICIAL WEBSITE; Amendments regarding Declaration of the injurious, unsafe or dangerous character of a consumer product; Regulation of unprocessed food; Breach of warranties; Repair service obligation; False, deceptive or misleading advertisement; Consumer complaints, and others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2019-07-31
